stem: Find the set of zeroes of the function $f(x)=x^3-4x^2$. Tap on the number line every value of $x$ for which $f(x)=0$.
solution: Factorise by taking out the common factor: $x^2(x-4)=0$.
Set each factor equal to zero: $x^2=0$ gives $x=0$; $x-4=0$ gives $x=4$.

hints.text: Every factor that can be zero gives a zero of the function. Check that you have set each factor equal to 0.
Substitute each value you marked into $f(x)$; it is a zero only if $f(x)$ comes out as 0.
Solve each factor equal to 0 again, carefully: in $x-a=0$, what must $x$ be?
